F (V) - Dominant turnaround resolving with authority

techniques.name: Vocal Melodic Phrasing & Wide Finger Vibrato
techniques.description: Brian May's singular approach of treating the guitar as an operatic tenor singer, emphasizing pitch accuracy, pre-bends, and wide, relaxed vibrato

notes: Played on the 'Red Special' guitar with a sixpence coin instead of a plastic pick
Features lyrical pre-bends that release downward smoothly into chord tones
Uses subtle finger vibrato that mimics a classical opera singer's throat vibrato
sequence: Slide smoothly into the target note
Execute a full 1-step bend with sustained reinforcement
Apply wide, singing finger vibrato after the bend reaches pitch
tips: Support your bending fingers with index and middle fingers behind the fretting finger
Use a coin or stiff heavy pick to emulate Brian May's percussive metallic chime

techniques.name: Multitracked Guitar Orchestration
techniques.description: Building three-part and four-part classical harmonies by layering individual guitar lines to simulate an entire brass or string orchestra

notes: Brian May layered multiple takes of the Red Special through a custom 'Deacy' amp
Employs parallel 3rds, 6ths, and contrary motion counterpoint
Out-of-phase pickup wiring creates the cutting, vocal midrange hollow honk
sequence: Layer harmonized line a diatonic 3rd above
Add third part an octave above or 6th below
tips: Dial treble booster in front of a mildly overdriven tube amp
Ensure zero tuning drift between takes—counterpoint turns harsh if slightly sharp

techniques.name: Double-Time Heavy Rock Riffing
techniques.description: Switching from lyrical ballad tempo to explosive 144 BPM heavy rock riffing with fast alternate picking and driving power chords

notes: The headbanging riff that kicks off the heavy section
Built around descending double-stop riffs in Eb and Bb
Demands precise right-hand muting and punchy accents
sequence: Rake descending triplet lick on D and G strings
Land hard on Bb5 power chord accent
tips: Dig into the strings with aggressive downstroke power
Let the amp naturally compress without adding muddy distortion

sections.name: Brian May Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Vocal Melodic Phrasing & Wide Finger Vibrato
sections.description: Considered one of the greatest guitar solos ever recorded: lyrical, emotional, and perfectly composed to advance the song's operatic narrative
sections.progression: Eb - Bb - Cm - Gm - Eb - Bb - Ab - Eb - F
notes: Begins with an expressive slide into the 8th fret on the G string
Features the famous ascending run through Bb major pentatonic with fast triplet flourishes
Ends on a soaring 1.5-step bend on the high E string (fret 18 to 21)

sections.name: Heavy Rock Headbanging Riff
sections.description: The roaring hard rock explosion immortalized in Wayne's World, shifting into double-time 144 BPM with punchy driving riffs
notes: Tempo shifts to 144 BPM with aggressive driving rock groove
Combine palm-muted pedal tones on the A string with open power chord stabs
Accentuate beat 1 of each bar with full-arm downstroke energy

guitar.recommended: Brian May Red Special or guitar with Burns Tri-Sonic pickups and phase switches
alternatives: Fender Stratocaster with out-of-phase pickup option
guitar.pickup: Bridge + Middle pickups wired in series and in-phase or out-of-phase for the nasal vocal solo tone

amp.recommended: Vox AC30 Top Boost paired with a Dallas Rangemaster Treble Booster
alternatives: Fender Twin Reverb with Treble Booster

effects.distortion: Treble Booster (Keeley Java Boost or Fryer Treble Booster) slamming the Vox AC30 front end
effects.reverb: Subtle analog spring or chamber reverb
effects.other: Sixpence coin used as a pick for metallic attack and harmonic scrapes

beginner.title: Learn Ballad Chord Changes & Hard Rock Riff
steps: Learn the core chord changes in Bb and Eb
Practice the heavy rock riff at a slow 100 BPM
Understand the multi-part structure of the song

intermediate.title: Master the Brian May Guitar Solo
steps: Learn the guitar solo note-for-note at 72 BPM
Focus on the lyrical pre-bends and pitch accuracy
Apply Brian May's singing finger vibrato on sustained notes

advanced.title: Orchestrated Harmonies & Complete Multi-Movement Performance
steps: Learn and record the three-part harmonized guitar layers
Master the transition into double-time 144 BPM heavy rock
Integrate treble booster tone shaping and out-of-phase pickup settings

commonMistakes: Bending out of tune on the lyrical solo—pitch accuracy is paramount on vocal-like lines
Using a floppy thin pick that fails to deliver Brian May's signature metallic chime
Rushing the transition into the heavy rock section—lock to the snare crack
practiceRoutine: 10 min: Pitch-accurate bending exercises in Bb and Eb major
15 min: Solo phrase isolation with focus on singing vibrato and pre-bends
15 min: Heavy rock section alternate picking and power chord tightness at 144 BPM
10 min: Complete run-through with original recording
focusAreas: Microtonal bend precision and vocal vibrato depth
Treble booster dynamic response using the guitar volume knob
Seamless tempo switching between 72 BPM and 144 BPM
metronomeWork: Practice the solo at 60 BPM with eighth-note clicks, gradually moving to 72 BPM
Practice the heavy riff starting at 110 BPM, stepping up to 144 BPM
